full_judgment:
"Let a rule be issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 11-3-2015 passed in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 911 of 2009 (Civil Revision No.654 of 2015) and Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 912 of 2009 (Civil Revision No.655 of 2015) should not be set aside, and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper". 

 3. Facts relevant are that the opposite party No. 1 (in both the civil revisions) invited international tender on 22-4-2009 and 27-7-2009 for importation of 1,25,000 Metric Tons and 62,500 Metric Tons Urea Fertilizer in bag respectively incorporating certain conditions in the tender schedule; The petitioner participated in both tenders by submitting Bank Guarantees along with other documents; Opposite Patty No.1 accepted offer of the petitioner and issued notification of award for both the bid with a condition, amongst others, to furnish performance guarantee (hereinafter called 'PG') at 10% of total CFR value within 6-8-2009; The petitioner prayed extension of time in writing for furnishing PG and the opposite party No.1 though allowed extension on three occasions but on 2-9-2009 rejecting the application for extension of time filed by the petitioner issued letter to the concern bank for encashment of the bank guarantees without settling the issue through arbitration as per Article 35.2(B) of the notification of award; On 11-5-2014, the petitioner amended the petition of Arbitration Miscellaneous Case and added after para 6 that the foreign principle refused to issue 10% PG since the amount is abnormally high and not in compliance with international common practice; Latter on the petitioner found that as per Public Procurement Regulation, the Bank Guarantee is to be submitted for divisible products like Urea Fertilizer at 5%, not at 10%; This fact was verbally brought to the notice of the opposite party No.1 and petitioner orally requested to reduce the amount of PG at 5%; Though concern officer of the opposite party No.1 verbally promised to settle the issue but ultimately did not as such the petitioner filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act praying for appointment of an arbitrator and referring the dispute for arbitration. 

 4. Opposite party No.1 contested the case by filing written statement contending inter alia that the petitioner participated in the international tender invited by the opposite party for procurement of urea fertilizer; The bid of the petitioner was accepted by the opposite party and accordingly notification of award was issued in favour of the petitioner asking to submit PG at 10% of the CFR value within 6-8-2009 and thereafter proceed for signing of the contract documents; Petitioner requested the opposite party by filing application for extension of time on 6-8-2009, 20-8-2009 and lastly on 27-82009 for furnishing PG and the opposite party allowed the application and lastly extended time till 1-9-2009 but on that date the petitioner again filed an application praying for further extension of time which was rejected and the opposite party withdrew the notification of award issued in favour of the petitioner and proceeded to forfeit the security as per ITT clause No.26,5 and notification of award clause No. VII; Since the parties did not execute any formal contact and there was no agreement for arbitration between the parties as such Arbitration Miscellaneous Case filed by the petitioner is misconceived and liable to be dismissed. 

 5. Upon hearing the parties and assessing materials on record, learned District Judge dismissed both the Miscellaneous Case on contest vide separate judgment and order dated 11-3-2015. 

 7. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner in both the Civil Revisions submits that the court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that article 35.2 of the notification of award contain the procedure for settlement of dispute through arbitration proceeding as such findings of the learned District Judge based on a wrong notion are liable to be set aside. He also submits that the court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the quantum of amount for furnishing PG specified in Public Procurement Regulation at 5% of CFR value for products like urea fertilizer which is also common international practice as such condition of furnishing PG at 10% as contained in the notification of award is in violation of the PPR and international norm which can only be resolved through arbitration proceeding under article 35.2 of the notification of award and, as such, impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He again submits that the court below committed an error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order without considering that the petitioner furnished bank guarantees to the tune of some crores as tender security and thus arbitration proceeding is necessary to resolve the dispute of PG amount under article 35.2 of the notification of award as such impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Wilson Smithett and Cape(Sugar) Ltd. vs Bangladesh Sugar and Food Industries Corporation, reported in Lloyd's Law Reports [QB (Corn) Ct 378]. 

 10. We have gone through the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned District Judge and the annexures appended with the application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure alongwith the application for stay. It appears that the petitioner participated in the international tender invited by the opposite party No. 1. The opposite party No.1 accepted offer of the petitioner and issued notification of award in favour of the petitioner on condition that after furnishing PG at 10% of the C.F.R. value a formal contract will be executed between the parties. It also appears that the petitioner filed three applications seeking extension of time for furnishing PG which were allowed by the opposite party extending time till 1-9-2009. On the very day, the petitioner again filed application for extension of time and then the opposite party No.1 rejected the application withdrewing notification of award and issued letter for encashment of bank guarantee. There after the petitioner raised the plea of Public Procurement Regulations and filed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act. Learned District Judge passed the impugned judgment and order on the application for appointment of an arbitrator under section 12 of the Arbitration Act. The moot question is whether in the circumstances narrated above application under section 12 is maintainable or not? In other words, whether the learned District Judge legally passed the impugned judgment and order dismissing the arbitration miscellaneous case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act. Admittedly, after accepting offer of the petitioner in the tender process, the opposite party issued notification of award in favour of the petitioner with a condition, amongst others, that a formal contract will be executed between the parties after furnishing PG at 10% of the CFR value by the petitioner. The whole argument of the learned advocate for the petitioner is that notification of award itself a contract and, as such, any dispute arose out of the contract has to be settled through arbitration proceeding under the Arbitration Act. We have to see whether this argument of the learned advocate has any legal basis. 

 12. Next to see that whether a 'notification of award' in the context of the case in hand is legally binding upon the parties. We find that in general terms, in many jurisdiction a notification of award confirms that a purchaser has accepted a bidder's proposal and agrees to proceed to a formal contract or purchase order. It's essentially a small step beyond a statement of intent but of formal contract. Such letters are typically not legally binding. 

 "since the parties failed to execute at a legally binding contract nor any party has acted under that contract giving rise to a dispute out of that contract I am unable to find any substance in the case of the petitioner". 

 16. It is admitted that no formal contract was executed between the parties and no agreement was signed by the parties under section 9 of the Arbitration Act, as such in our opinion the learned District Judge justly and legally passed the impugned judgment and order dismissing the arbitration miscellaneous case filed under section 12 of the Arbitration Act. We are not inclined to go into the details whether the petitioner participated in the bid by filing tender submitting that he will abide by the conditions contained in the tender schedule. In a case under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, it is to be seen whether the parties signed any agreement for arbitration proceeding under section 9 of the Arbitration Act. Since no formal contract executed between the parties and no written agreement has been signed by the parties for arbitration proceeding, learned District Judge justly and legally passed the impugned judgment and order dismissing the application under section 12 of the Arbitration Act and thereby committed no error of law which occasioned failure of justice. 

 17. We have gone through the judgment cited by the learned advocate for the petitioner reported in Lloyd's Law Reports [QB (Com) Ct 378]. This judgment has no relevancy with the facts and circumstances of the case in hand rather this citation shows un-mindfulness of the learned advocate for the petitioner. 

 19. Judgment and order dated 11-3-2015 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka, in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case Nos. 911 of 2009 and 912 of 2009 respectively are maintained.
